full_judgment:
7. Title suit 71 of 1976 of the contesting defendant was a suit for declaration that the order passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue) on 24.11.1973 in Redemption Case 2 of 1973, is illegal, without jurisdiction and for permanent injunction. Present suit is for redemption of mortgage and for khas Possession and for declaration that the decree passed on 31.12.76 in Title Suit 71 of 1976 is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. Not only cause of action and Subject matter are different but also issues are completely different. So there was no scope for final decision by the former court in respect of the present subject matter, pending for decision in the present suit. Therefor I find that the decision in Title Suit 71 of 1976 is not bar, by resjudicata, in deciding the present suit. The decision in title suit 71 of 1976 is not a legal decision. So it is not binding upon the plaintiff. Mr. J.N. Dev, the learned Counsel for the petitioner pursuaded me to go through the decision in the case of Mathura Prasad Sarjoo Jaiswal and others Vs. Dossibai N.B.Jeejeebhoy, AIR 1971(SC) 2355 in support of his submission that the present suit will not be barred by resjudicata. In that case, their Lordships have opined in para 9 on resjudica as follows:- 

 9. The result, therefor is, that the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgments and decrees of the courts below are set aside. The suit of the plaintiff-petitioner being Title suit 83 of 1989 is decreed declaring that the mortgage has been redeemped and the plaintiff is entitled to get khas possession of the suit land by executing the decree against the defendant and that the decree passed in Title Suit 71 of 1976 is no more binding upon the petitioner.
